chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Abu Ismail al-Sarraj, from Harun ibn Kharja, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The one who is buried in the Haram (sanctuary) will be secure from the Great Panic (on the Day of Judgment).' So I said to him, 'From the righteous of the people and their immoral ones (as well)?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'From the righteous of the people and their immoral ones (as well)'.

key_terms.الْحَرَم: The Sanctuary (referring to the shrine of an Imam)
key_terms.الْفَزَعِ الْأَكْبَرِ: The Great Panic (a specific event on the Day of Judgment)

ai.seo_question: Does burial in the Imam's shrine guarantee safety from the Great Panic for all the dead?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) confirms that burial within the sacred precincts (Haram) of the Imams ensures deliverance from the 'Great Panic' (al-Faz' al-Akbar) on the Day of Judgment. The Imam’s repetition of 'from the righteous and the wicked' emphasizes that this intercessory merit is not contingent upon the individual's personal piety but is a universal benefit conferred by proximity to the Ahl al-Bayt. This reflects the Shia theological principle of the sanctity of the Imams' resting places as sources of divine mercy and intercession.
